title: Length-harmonic continuous batcher and KV compaction playbook
creator: Samir Rao
description:
Goal: produce a reproducible playbook and production-safe patchset that reduces p99 latency regressions and GPU memory fragmentation for mixed-length prompt/response workloads by harmonically normalizing batch admission and coordinating KV compaction watermarks. Scope includes scheduler heuristics (admission + aging), adaptive prefetch windows, KV shard compaction triggers, and an in-host GPU allocator hinting flow. We will prioritize minimal risk changes that can be feature-flagged and rolled back.

Background: mixed prompt/response workloads show heavy tail behavior (short prompts that generate long responses and vice versa). Current continuous batcher admits disparate sequence lengths into the same slot-tenure buckets which increases KV residency churn and causes transient GPU slab fragmentation, increasing peak memory and p99. Early simulation shows a 14% p99 increase during asymmetric-dialogue bursts and up to 9% higher GPU footer usage under realistic production traces.

Approach: first perform controlled experiments in the perf harness (perf-runner branch) with: 1) harmonic length normalization: compute harmonic mean of token lengths across candidate coalescing window and use as soft admission score to prefer near-harmonic groups; 2) adaptive prefetch window: increase prefetch depth for cohorts where KV hit probability > 0.65 and conversely shrink for low-hit cohorts; 3) compaction watermarks per-KV-shard: trigger slab compaction only when resident ration delta > 0.12 and GPU free memory drops below 7%; 4) allocator hinting: expose a lightweight hint from the scheduler to the GPU allocator to prefer contiguous slab reuse for same-cohort batches.

Deliverables: playbook doc with knobs/expected tradeoffs, feature-flagged runtime patch, perf dashboards comparing baseline vs tuned, rollout plan (canary + controlled ramp), and rollback steps.

Notes on risk: compaction is expensive and can increase tail if run naively — hence watermarks are tuned conservatively. Allocator hints require careful testing with multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

Operational metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU memory high-water mark, KV hit ratio, slot churn rate, cold-start cache misses, and cost-per-100k-tokens.

This ticket is primarily an engineering experiment plus small runtime changes; product/console changes are out of scope but we will add visibility tiles for the tuned knobs in the Optimize dashboard if results are positive.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency reduced by >=6% on asymmetric-dialogue benchmark under target load
GPU peak memory reduced by >=5% on production trace replay
no >3% increase in p50 latency across control cohort during canary
feature behind runtime feature-flag and rollbackable within 10 minutes
automated perf tests added to CI and dashboards created for the knobs
comments: 2026-02-12 - Spike complete: implemented harmonic scoring in perf-runner (branch: perf/length-harmonic). Simulated 8% improvement in p99 for medium-burst traces. Observed higher admission oscillation in long-turn dominated traces; added dampening factor to admission score.

2026-02-18 - Internal design review with SRE and allocator team. Agreement to surface an opaque hint (enum: CONTIGUOUS_PREFER) rather than allocator API changes. SRE requested safety valve to disable compaction during I/O-heavy maintenance windows.

2026-02-25 - Experiment #1: harmonic-only in canary pool (10% traffic). Result: p99 down 5.2% overall, but a minority customer flow saw +7% p95 due to aggressive grouping; adjusted admission threshold and re-ran locally.

2026-03-02 - Experiment #2: harmonic + adaptive-prefetch + conservative compaction watermarks in perf replay. Peak GPU memory down 6.8%, KV hit ratio up 3.9%. During an induced microburst, compaction triggered twice causing a 9% p99 spike; added throttle to limit compaction frequency to once per 30s per shard.
2026-03-06 - PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1478 (contains scheduler changes + feature-flag). Requesting review from @maria-keller (allocator) and @jonah-lee (scheduling).

2026-03-09 - Design feedback: Maria requested more observability for compaction events (emit compact_start/compact_end trace events and attach shard_id + pre/post-residency). Jonah suggested exposing a fast path for single-turn short prompts where harmonic normalization is skipped to avoid regression for latency-sensitive microcalls.

2026-03-12 - Canary ramp: 25% traffic for 6 hours in eu-west. Metrics: p99 -6.4%, GPU HWM -5.6%. One alert for compaction throttle reached in a spike window; engineering on-call added temporary mute and will follow up to tune thresholds.

2026-03-14 - Today's status: resolving two issues before broader rollout: (1) add fast-path skip for single-turn <32 token prompts, (2) persist per-shard last-compaction timestamp to avoid double-compaction across restarts. Expected next update 2026-03-18 after small patch and an A/B run.
open_questions: What is the safe minimum interval between compaction runs per shard under high churn?
Should we expose harmonic admission alpha as a customer-visible knob for Dedicated customers or keep it experimentation-only?
Can allocator hints be implemented purely in userspace without kernel or driver changes for on-prem deployments?
next_steps: Complete small runtime patch for fast-path skip and last-compaction persistence (ETA 2026-03-17)
Run 48-hour A/B test against control on staging using replayed multi-tenant traces (ETA 2026-03-20)
If A/B passes, prepare rollout playbook and change control for canary to 50% then 100% with hourly monitoring windows
Document knobs and expected tradeoffs in Optimize playbook and add visibility tile to Console
